title: Compact completed history before a multi-tool turn crosses its context reserve
hypothesis: Checking the reserve before every model call and compacting only completed history will let an active edit/test turn survive a context boundary without losing the latest correction or splitting tool protocol, while adding no work below the boundary.
falsified_if: The treatment loses the corrected values, scope restriction, active tool exchange, or verification; fails to avoid the injected hard boundary; or adds compaction/model calls to the below-boundary simple prompt.
local_evidence: LCA's REPL checked automatic compaction only after core.run_session returned, while one run_session can perform up to forty model/tool steps. Compaction also retained usage metadata tied to the replaced message indices.
decision_rule: Reject on any treatment loss of the latest correction, scope, active-turn protocol, or verification. Accept the reserve check only if every boundary treatment run completes, boundary controls reproducibly stop at the injected limit, and neither simple-prompt variant compacts or adds model/tool calls. The artificial small limit validates boundary behavior, not real 200k-token latency or summary quality at full scale.
